title: Slice sensitivity: int4 vs int8 case notes and follow-ups
body:
Purpose:
Quick working notes from the most recent quantization-impact run focused on slice-level sensitivity. This is a capture of observed deltas, odd failure modes, and short-term mitigations we can land before the next onboarding batch. Not a polished report — treat as an engineering scratchpad.

Summary (top-line):
- Baseline: fp16 / bf16 model (family: rwd-13B-v2) served in reference config.
- Candidates: AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int4, AWQ-int8 (and a gated int8 quant profile).
- Evaluation scope: ~12k prompts across 6 slices (defined below). Metrics: task accuracy / correctness, semantic-sim (embedding cosine to reference), fluency regressions (LM perplexity proxy), and safety trigger delta.
- Headline: AWQ-int4 shows the largest mean quality drop (-3.4% task accuracy overall) but variance is slice-dependent. GPTQ-int4 is slightly less regressive (-1.7% overall) but still has concentrated regressions on arithmetic and long-context slices. Int8 profiles are within noise for most slices (<=0.6% delta) and are the safest option for production-sensitive workloads.

Slice definitions used in this run (short):
- instruction-following: multi-step natural language tasks, chain-of-thoughts encouraged.
- math/arithmetic: short to medium-length numeric problems, symbolic reasoning.
- code-generation: small function synthesis, unit-test checkable output.
- long-context: >4k token context retrieval / summarization prompts.
- knowledge-fact: fact lookup / closed-answer prompts where exactness matters.
- safety-sensitive: prompts crafted to probe policy boundaries and hallucination/unsafe outputs.

Key numeric deltas (relative to fp16 baseline). these are median deltas across prompt subsets; use as directional not absolute.
- instruction-following: AWQ-int4 -3.8% accuracy; GPTQ-int4 -1.9%; AWQ-int8 -0.4%
- math/arithmetic: AWQ-int4 -6.5% accuracy; GPTQ-int4 -4.2%; AWQ-int8 -1.1%
- code-generation: AWQ-int4 -8.6% pass@1 (unit-test proxy); GPTQ-int4 -5.0%; AWQ-int8 -0.8%
- long-context: AWQ-int4 -5.2% coherence score; GPTQ-int4 -3.0%; AWQ-int8 -0.9%
- knowledge-fact: AWQ-int4 -2.2% exact-match; GPTQ-int4 -0.9%; AWQ-int8 -0.2%
- safety-sensitive: AWQ-int4 +0.6% safety triggers (worse); GPTQ-int4 +0.3%; AWQ-int8 +0.05%

Observed failure modes (concrete examples):
1) Tokenized numeric drift: for certain arithmetic prompts, AWQ-int4 produced numerically-plausible but incorrect intermediate steps (e.g., mis-summed terms). Hypothesis: quantization noise changes softmax mass distribution causing different attention weights on numeric tokens.
2) Code token truncation / bracket mismatch: AWQ-int4 occasionally emits malformed code with missing closing tokens when the prompt includes uncommon operator sequences. GPTQ-int4 less affected but still visible for tricky language subsets.
3) Long-context coherence drop: in >6k token summarization tests, AWQ-int4 tends to repeat head phrases and lose reference links; KV-cache numerical stability under AWQ-int4 suspected.
4) Safety triggers: small increase in hallucinated persona claims on AWQ-int4 in a handful of adversarial prompts. Not catastrophic but notable for enterprise safety policy.

Diagnostics we ran:
- Per-layer activation distribution comparison (fp16 vs AWQ-int4) on a 500-example slice sample. Observed notable kurtosis increase in mid-attention layers for AWQ-int4.
- KV-cache checksum comparison: mismatch rate higher on int4 configurations, aligned with long-context regressions.
- Embedding cosine drift: mean embedding similarity for AWQ-int4 dropped 0.012 absolute vs fp16 on the knowledge-fact slice (small but consistent).

Immediate recommendations (short-term / low lift):
- Default to int8 AWQ for onboarding customers that have code/math/long-context heavy workloads. Int8 keeps cost benefits while avoiding the larger drops we see in int4.
- Gate AWQ-int4 behind a canary and only enable for non-critical accounts until we finish mitigation experiments. Suggested rollout: 5% traffic, monitoring window 48h, automatic rollback on >1.5% accuracy regression on a chosen canary promptset (see linked_artifacts).
- Add slice-specific threshold checks to the onboarding pipeline: during preflight, compute slice deltas vs baseline and fail onboarding if any slice delta exceeds configured limits (defaults: math >3%, code >4%, long-context >3%).
- Improve prompt-set coverage for arithmetic and code: add ~1k hard instances sourced from internal bug reports and OSS test suites (see APL-2219).

Longer-term mitigations / experiments to prioritize:
- Quant-aware fine-tuning (QAT) on a mixed-loss objective weighted towards math/code slices. Small warm-start QAT could be low-cost and targeted.
- Per-token calibration tables for AWQ-int4 to reduce numeric drift for common subtoken sequences (prototype idea from Ethan; see PR #78).
- KV-cache numeric stabilization patch: investigate using higher-precision accumulation for KV updates in long-context mode. Benchmark cost vs quality tradeoffs.
- Explore hybrid-decoding strategy: use int4 for prefix/short responses but switch to int8 when model detects numeric/code tokens; needs runtime support but may give best of both.

Canary plan (concrete):
1) Create canary cluster with AWQ-int4 behind feature flag.
2) Deploy to 5% of dev/test traffic with strict logging of slice-level metrics and example retention.
3) Run rolling experiments for 72h, compare against baseline int8 canary.
4) If any slice breaches the thresholds (see above), automatic rollback and gather failure exemplars for analysis.
Responsible: Marjorie Liu (deploy), Ethan Park (monitoring alerts), Priya Nambiar (analysis).

Outstanding questions / open actions:
- Should we expand the safety-sensitive slice to include adversarial prompt mutations? (Carlos to propose a short set by 2025-03-05)
- Decide default quant profile for newly-onboarded customers in the console: opt-in int4 vs opt-out (product decision required).
- Run a targeted QAT pilot on 1B parameter subset to validate ROI timeline.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Might be useful to instrument token-level confidence (softmax max) drift as a lightweight proxy for regression detection in real-time.
- Keep a small "golden set" of unit-testable code prompts for each model family; this caught the largest code regressions in this run.

Appendix: quick artifact links and example failure IDs (for triage)
- Example fail (instruction-following): FAIL-ID: APL-2025-ff1 (attached in GH gist link in PR #78)
- Example code fail: FAIL-ID: APL-2025-c23 (unit-test diff + stacktrace saved in S3: s3://redwood-qa/quant-fails/2025-02-10/)

If you're reviewing: add notes inline or ping me in #applied-ml. Will convert to a formal regression report if product asks for a customer-facing summary.

-- Priya
